description: Review of the names_match / RFC 4518 normalization implementation in pkix-path/src/lib.rs
notes: Confidence: 20% chance of missed bug. Reasoning: The implementation is tight and well-structured. The one P1 real finding (PKIX-doy) is a maintainer-burden risk around undocumented SET-matching invariant — that is real but not a latent bug in the current code. The P2 findings are mostly correct architectural decisions documented as such (PKIX-3gk, PKIX-k7s, PKIX-b2a, PKIX-2ld, PKIX-kqj). The P2 documentation/maintainer tasks (PKIX-43q, PKIX-fdk, PKIX-2xm) are genuine but low-severity. The only P3 under this epic (PKIX-h8b) has a factually incorrect premise: any_to_str_bytes returns None WITHOUT calling value(), so the fallback value() calls in (None, None) branch are first-access not redundant — labeled opinion. Primary residual risk: the NormalizedIter pending_space state machine correctness for leading/trailing space stripping — possible edge case with strings that are all whitespace (would emit nothing, correct) or strings with only a single interior space (correct). Tested with unit tests but PKITS §4.4 DN matching vectors not yet run. Running out of real complaints: yes.
title: Review round 1: RFC 4518 DN normalization (PKIX-pyc)
